text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — ran a focused nsys/profile on the 2ms continuous-batching change. Seeing a recurring queue-tail spike that lines up with a burst of tiny matmul/cublas launches. nsys trace uploaded to s3 and perfetto link in the run log.
Ari: can you drop the top hotspots? :eyes:
Sam: perf-bot posted the summary (trimmed):
perf-bot: TOP_KERNELS: small_matmul_k=38.7% (many ~300-900us launches), soft_kernel_dispatch=22.3%, kv_cache_sweep=9.1%, cuda_memcpy=6.4%
Sam: Also noticed ~1.6ms windows where GPU is saturated and then a 1.2-2.5ms stall in host queues before next batch launches. pattern repeats per request batch.
Maria: that kv_cache_sweep at 1.2s in the trace — is it a global sweep or per-shard? Could be evictions causing extra host-side work.
Luis: I suspect the scheduler wakes too aggressively for small inflight token counts. combo of aggressive kernel selection (favoring many small matmuls) + 2ms window -> high per-launch overhead.
Ari: do you have the capture command so I can repro locally?
Sam: yup, used this:
```
sys profile --stats true --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn --sample=none -o cont_batch_2ms --sleep 0 --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- python -m perfrun --workload=kv-heavy
```
Sam: perfetto view: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (host timeline + gpu kernel waterfall). pulls out ~6800 kernel launches in 60s segment.
Maria: quick numbers from a short sim:
- window=2ms: median p99 latency 42ms / queue-time contribution ~45% (host wait + dispatch)
- window=4ms: median 44ms / queue-time 28%
- window=6ms: median 47ms / queue-time 18% (but CPU tail increases a bit)
Luis: so increasing window reduces queue/time ratio but increases median compute wait due to larger batches. tradeoff seems clear.
Ari: alternative: tune kernel selection to prefer fused/macro kernels when sequence len < 64 to reduce number of launches. Have we tried target kernel affinity?
Sam: not for this model. current kernel selector picks matmul path A for perf, but there is a larger batched matmul path that triggers only if seq_len > 80. we could loosen that threshold.
Maria: also saw KV cache sweep triggered by mem_pressure signal from our async GC. If we stagger sweeps by shard or rate-limit sweep job it might smooth host spikes.
ops-bot: FYI — current Dedicated pool autoscaler was nudged at 12:30 for load spike, not related to these micro spikes.
Sam: proposal: 1) run A/B with window=2ms vs 6ms on synthetic load for 30min with nsys + perfetto capture (50k tokens), 2) prototype kernel-selector tweak to prefer fused matmul for seq<80, 3) rate-limit kv-cache sweeps to <1 sweep/sec per shard and run nsys again.
Ari: +1. I'll own the kernel-selector tweak and a deterministic micro-benchmark to validate launch counts.
Maria: I'll re-run the kv-sweep code with rate-limiting and add event markers into perfetto to correlate.
Luis: I'll set up the A/B experiment in staging and hook the release flag. route 10% traffic to the 6ms variant.
Sam: Logged an internal perf ticket: PERF-1193 with links to traces & the sim numbers. I'll attach the nsys archive and perfetto ID.
Ari: any quick wins before the full experiment? maybe drop small launch path temporarily to see impact.
Sam: I can flip a runtime flag to prefer the fused matmul for a quick smoke. Will do on staging now. ping when done.
Luis: staging flip applied, smoke run looks promising — kernel launch count down ~35% and GPU active duty slightly higher but less host queueing.
Maria: nice. let's collect 10m of nsys and ship to the perf team for deeper analysis.
Sam: thanks all — will follow up in PERF-1193 with artifacts. :thumbsup:
